15: # Figma CLI Tool Surface
16: 
17: > **IMPORTANT:** This taxonomy was built from a read-only source scan of the silships `figma-cli` repo (`main`, package `figma-ds-cli@1.2.0`) plus its `REFERENCE.md` / `CLAUDE.md`. The command surface **drifts** between `REFERENCE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, and the actual `src/commands/*.js` (documented commands such as `voice`, `chat`, `prop combine`, and the `create rect/circle/...` primitives were NOT found in the source scan). **Always verify a command with `<bin> <command> --help` before relying on it**, and gate every mutating or destructive verb. The CLI was not installed or executed during this analysis, so every example below is **illustrative, so verify with `--help`**.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ## 1. OVERVIEW
22: 
23: ### Purpose
24: 
25: This reference lets a reader classify any `figma-ds-cli` command and apply the matching gate before it runs.
26: 
27: ### When to Use
28: 
29: - Decide whether a `figma-ds-cli` command is safe to call unprompted, must be gated, or is destructive and needs confirmation plus a rollback.
30: - Confirm the gating class of any command before authoring, modifying, deleting, or exporting in a Figma document.
31: - Reach for the destructive set and rollback table before any delete / clear / undo / unwrap / uninstall / unlink operation.
32: 
33: ### Core Principle
34: 
35: Surface read-only commands freely, gate every mutating verb behind confirmation plus an explicit target plus a one-line rollback, treat the explicit destructive set as the strictest case (confirm + explicit target + rollback, prefer duplicate-first), and treat `eval` / `raw` / `run` as arbitrary mutation that must be reviewed before it runs. The canonical binary is **`figma-ds-cli`**, and the source surface is the only source of truth and it drifts from the docs.
36: 
37: ### Key Sources
38: 
39: - [figma-cli-reference.md](figma-cli-reference.md) - the binary identity, connect modes, daemon model, and command examples.
40: - [mcp-wiring.md](mcp-wiring.md) - the optional Framelink Figma MCP via Code Mode (a separate, opt-in surface, not part of this CLI gating).
41: 
42: Claims here are tagged **READ-ONLY**, **MUTATING**, **DESTRUCTIVE**, or **ARBITRARY** as defined in Section 2, and were read from a source scan of the silships figma-cli during the skill's build research. They are **source-verified for repo `main`**, not live-verified against an installed binary.
43: 
44: ### The naming trap (read first)
45: 
46: The canonical binary is **`figma-ds-cli`** (silships, npm `figma-ds-cli`, MIT). The npm package literally named **`figma-cli` is an UNRELATED tool** (unic/figma-cli, bin `figma`). **NEVER `npm i -g figma-cli`.** The `figma-cli` command only exists when installed from the silships repo (`main` exposes both `figma-ds-cli` and `figma-cli`), while npm `latest` (`1.0.0`) exposes only `figma-ds-cli`. This document writes every command with `figma-ds-cli`.
47: 
48: ---
49: 
50: ## 2. THE FOUR CLASSES
51: 
52: Every command falls into exactly one gating class. The class drives the exposure policy in Section 4.
53: 
54: - **READ-ONLY**: reads Figma or local state, or writes an **export file**, without changing the Figma document or app/config state. Safe to surface. **Caveat:** any command that writes a local file (`extract`, `export*`, `verify --save`, `analyze-url --screenshot`, `api setup/index`) must use an **explicit output path and never silently overwrite** an existing file (see Section 5).
55: - **MUTATING**: changes the Figma document, the current selection, or local tool / app / plugin / config state. Gate behind confirmation + an explicit target + a one-line rollback. Includes all authoring, layout, token, binding, variant, import, app-level connect/patch/daemon, and `init-agent` verbs.
56: - **DESTRUCTIVE**: deletes Figma document content, variables, collections, annotations, grids, or removes an installed/local resource. The strictest case: confirm + **explicit target** + a stated rollback, and **prefer duplicating** the file/page/selection first. Never via an active-selection fallback. The explicit set + per-command rollback is Section 6.
57: - **ARBITRARY**: `eval`, `run`, and `raw` execute arbitrary Figma Plugin API code or arbitrary `figma-use` commands. They can do **anything** (read, mutate, or delete). Treat as MUTATING-at-minimum, **review the code/command before running**, and never run them on an exploratory hunch (Section 7).
58: 
59: > Tag meanings used in the table below: `READ-ONLY`, `MUTATING`, `DESTRUCTIVE`, `ARBITRARY`. Where a single command name has read-only and write sub-verbs (`component prop`, `dev`, `section`, `grid`, `annotate`), the per-sub-verb class is called out.
60: 
61: ---
62: 
63: ## 3. THE COMMAND SURFACE (CLASSIFIED BY GROUP)
64: 
65: Source-verified against repo `main` `src/commands/*.js`, `REFERENCE.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`. **Verify with `--help` before relying on any row**, since the surface drifts (Section 8).
66: 
67: | Group | Command | Class | Notes |
68: | ----- | ------- | ----- | ----- |
69: | Setup | `figma-ds-cli` (first run) | MUTATING | First-run wizard: checks Node, may patch Figma, starts Figma. App-level. |
70: | Setup | `init` / `setup` | MUTATING | Interactive setup; `setup` aliases `init`. App-level. |
71: | Setup | `connect [--safe]` | MUTATING | `--safe` = plugin bridge (no patch, DEFAULT). Bare `connect` = yolo `app.asar` patch (GATE: consent + rollback). App-level. |
72: | Setup | `unpatch` | MUTATING | Restores the original `app.asar` string (the yolo rollback). App-level. |
73: | Setup | `status` | READ-ONLY | Checks CDP + daemon status. |
74: | Setup | `diagnose` | READ-ONLY | System compatibility + connection status. |
75: | Daemon | `daemon status [--debug]` | READ-ONLY | Daemon health / token diagnostics. |
76: | Daemon | `daemon diagnose` | READ-ONLY | Full daemon troubleshooting. |
77: | Daemon | `daemon start [--force]` | MUTATING | Starts daemon, generates token. App-level. |
78: | Daemon | `daemon stop` | MUTATING | Stops daemon. App-level. |
79: | Daemon | `daemon restart` | MUTATING | Restarts daemon, regenerates token. App-level. |
80: | Daemon | `daemon reconnect` | MUTATING | Reconnects daemon to Figma. App-level. |

301: **Fix**:
302: 
303: ```bash
304: # Revert to a known-clean bundle first, then re-establish the connection.
305: figma-ds-cli unpatch        # illustrative; restore the original app.asar

308: ```
309: 
310: ---
311: 
312: ## 7. DAEMON ISSUES
313: 
314: The daemon is a local HTTP server, not a Unix socket:
315: 
316: - **Endpoint**: `127.0.0.1:3456`.
317: - **Auth**: the `X-Daemon-Token` header (`~/.figma-ds-cli/.daemon-token`).
318: - **PID file**: `~/.figma-cli-daemon.pid`.
319: - **Lifetime**: an idle timeout (~60 min), with no reboot persistence.
320: 
321: Recovery order is always **status -> diagnose -> restart -> reconnect**.
322: 
323: ### Issue: daemon "Unauthorized"
324: 
325: **Symptoms**:
326: 
327: ```bash
328: $ figma-ds-cli daemon status
329: Unauthorized
330: ```
331: 
332: **Cause**: Token mismatch between the client and the running daemon (`X-Daemon-Token`).
333: 
334: > **Never auto-delete the token** (`~/.figma-ds-cli/.daemon-token`) and never print its contents in user-facing output. Diagnose, then restart, because deletion is not the remedy.
335: 
336: **Fix**:
337: 
338: ```bash
339: figma-ds-cli daemon diagnose 2>&1   # inspect the mismatch first
340: figma-ds-cli daemon restart 2>&1    # restart re-aligns the token
341: ```
342:

345: ### Issue: daemon unreachable on port 3456
346: 
347: **Symptoms**: Daemon-backed commands hang or fail to connect to `127.0.0.1:3456`.
348: 
349: **Diagnosis**:
350: 
351: ```bash
352: figma-ds-cli daemon status 2>&1
353: ls -l ~/.figma-cli-daemon.pid 2>/dev/null   # is a daemon recorded?
354: lsof -nP -iTCP:3456 -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null # who, if anyone, owns 3456
355: ```
356: 
357: **Causes**:
358: 
359: - The daemon idled out (~60 min), since it is not reboot-persistent.
360: - The daemon crashed.
361: - Another process holds port 3456.
362: 
363: **Fix**:
364: 
365: 1. **Idle / crashed**: `figma-ds-cli daemon restart` (then `daemon reconnect` if the bridge is up but the document link dropped).
366: 2. **Port owned by another process**: identify the owner with `lsof` first, and **never blind-kill** the port. If it is a stale figma-ds-cli daemon, `daemon restart`, but otherwise resolve the owning process before reusing 3456.

312: ## 7. DAEMON ISSUES
313: 
314: The daemon is a local HTTP server, not a Unix socket:
315: 
316: - **Endpoint**: `127.0.0.1:3456`.
317: - **Auth**: the `X-Daemon-Token` header (`~/.figma-ds-cli/.daemon-token`).
318: - **PID file**: `~/.figma-cli-daemon.pid`.

323: ### Issue: daemon "Unauthorized"
324: 
325: **Symptoms**:
326:

329: Unauthorized
330: ```

332: **Cause**: Token mismatch between the client and the running daemon (`X-Daemon-Token`).
333:

335:

337: 
338: ```bash
339: figma-ds-cli daemon diagnose 2>&1   # inspect the mismatch first
340: figma-ds-cli daemon restart 2>&1    # restart re-aligns the token
341: ```

## 1. OVERVIEW

Requests reach this skill when they name `clickup` or `cupt` with a task action such as list, show, done, note, time, tag or context, when they mention a work queue, time tracking, a ClickUp document, a workspace search, an install or auth question, or a ClickUp failure. It routes to four resource families:

- `references/cupt-commands.md` for the CLI's daily operations
- `references/mcp-tools.md` for the hosted MCP's task, document, search, list, relation, chat and reminder tools
- `INSTALL-GUIDE.md` with `references/troubleshooting.md` for setup and auth
- `references/troubleshooting.md` alone for a failure report

The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
loads before an intent selects it.

---

## 2. INTENT MODEL

- **`CUPT_DAILY`** (weight 5) fires on the daily cupt phrasing, "list", "show", "done", "mark done", "complete task", "my tasks", "due today", "overdue", "log time", "start timer", "add a comment", "work queue" and "task details". It loads `references/cupt-commands.md`, and nothing else.
- **`MCP_ADVANCED`** (weight 5) fires on "create a task", "subtask", "document", "doc page", "search clickup", "manage lists", "task dependencies", "chat", "reminder" and "move task", and the MCP-only phrasings in `MCP_ONLY_PHRASES` select it whenever an error or install signal does not outrank them. It loads `references/mcp-tools.md`.
- **`INSTALL`** (weight 6) fires on "install cupt", "setup", "not installed", "auth", "authenticate", "api token", "mcp config", "sign in" and "how do i install", and a score above 4 selects it, unless `TROUBLESHOOT` also scores above 3, which the machine router checks first. It loads `INSTALL-GUIDE.md` and `references/troubleshooting.md`, because a setup request usually ends in a failure report.
=== mobbin
---

## 1. OVERVIEW

A Mobbin request reaches this skill when it names Mobbin, or asks for real app screenshots, app design research, UX flow references, screen examples from shipped apps, or the wiring, auth, plan gating and rate-limit troubleshooting of the registered `mobbin` manual, while generic design, UI or screen wording does not. From there the router selects among three reference families and one asset: the live three-tool contract and query-intent workflows in `references/tool-surface.md`, the registered manual, bridge and auth model in `references/mcp-wiring.md`, the failure modes in `references/troubleshooting.md`, and the registered manual's reference shape in `assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`, because this is a flat intent router with no keyed resource subdirectories. `references/tool-surface.md` is the declared default, offered as a fallback suggestion and never unioned into a scored route's loaded set; a scored route loads only the files its `RESOURCE_MAP` entry names.

The router answers one question: given a request, which skill-local resources load, in what order, and
what happens when nothing matches. Every path below stays inside this skill folder, and no resource
loads before an intent selects it.

---

## 2. INTENT MODEL

Six intents, one per `INTENT_SIGNALS` key, and each names the phrasing that fires it and the exact files its `RESOURCE_MAP` entry loads.

- **`APPS`**: "app design research", "app research", "competitor", "app comparison", "banking apps", "category", "how do apps" or "real apps" loads `references/tool-surface.md`.
- **`SCREENS`**: "screen", "screen examples", "ui pattern", "empty state", "first open", "onboarding screen", "component example", "screenshot", "paywall", "settings" or "dashboard" loads `references/tool-surface.md`.
- **`FLOWS`**: "flow", "ux flow", "user flow", "journey", "start to finish", "multi-step", "progression", "forgot password", "checkout" or "signup process" loads `references/tool-surface.md`.
- **`ELEMENTS`**: "element", "bottom sheet", "inline validation", "component behavior", "button state", "tab bar", "modal" or "confirmation dialog" loads `references/tool-surface.md`.
- **`WIRING_AUTH`**: "wiring", "utcp", "oauth", "mcp-remote", "authenticate", "pkce", "manual", "register", "token", "plan", "install" or "setup" loads `references/mcp-wiring.md` and `assets/utcp-mobbin-manual.md`.
- **`TROUBLESHOOT`**: "error", "failed", "401", "not working", "not resolving", "429", "rate limit", "timeout", "unauthorized" or "denied" loads `references/troubleshooting.md` and `references/mcp-wiring.md`.

28: Copy the line below into the project `.env`, replace the placeholder with a Figma personal access token (Figma → Settings → Account → Personal Access Tokens), and never commit `.env`. The manual entry that consumes this key lives in [utcp-figma-manual.md](./utcp-figma-manual.md).

27:

29: 
30: Add the manual object below into the `manual_call_templates` array of the project's `.utcp_config.json`, then put the prefixed key in `.env` (see [env-template.md](./env-template.md)). Code Mode names the manual `figma`, so calls are `figma.figma_<tool>` via `call_tool_chain()`, and the env var is prefixed `figma_`. 39: - The server needs a Figma personal access token, referenced as `${FIGMA_API_KEY}` and supplied in `.env` as `figma_FIGMA_API_KEY`.

52:         "command": "npx",

# scripts: Figma MCP Setup, Connect, and Diagnostics

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

`scripts/` holds the setup, connect, daemon, and diagnostic scripts for `mcp-figma`, the Figma transport mode of the `mcp-tooling` hub. Every script except `_common.sh` and `print-utcp-snippets.sh` sources `_common.sh` for its color helpers, its `figma_bin` resolver and its daemon paths, so all scripts that resolve `figma-ds-cli` agree on how to find the canonical binary. `print-utcp-snippets.sh` only prints static Code Mode wiring text, so it never needs those helpers. The canonical package is `figma-ds-cli` (the silships tool). A bare `figma` command belongs to the unrelated npm package `unic/figma-cli` and none of these scripts select it.

# figma-cli

> The silships figma-cli embedded in the mcp-figma skill. Published to npm as `figma-ds-cli`, it drives Figma Desktop from the terminal (read, author, modify, and export designs, tokens, and components) over a local daemon, with no Figma API key.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

`figma-ds-cli` is the silships terminal tool that gives a coding agent or operator direct control of an open Figma Desktop file: reading structure, authoring frames and components, managing tokens and variables, and exporting assets and code, all without a Figma API key. It talks to Figma over a local daemon rather than the REST API, so the live Desktop session is the source of truth.

# mcp-figma: Feature Catalog

This document is the canonical capability inventory for the `mcp-figma` skill. The root catalog acts as the system-level directory: it summarizes each capability area, names the canonical `figma-ds-cli` command for each feature, and tags every command read-only, mutating, or destructive so the gating model is visible at a glance. The skill drives the installed Figma Desktop app from the terminal through the silships `figma-ds-cli` so a coding agent can connect, inspect, author, modify, and export designs, tokens, and components, and **optionally** pull design context out of Figma through a community Figma MCP via Code Mode. The CLI is the primary surface, and the MCP is opt-in.

> **Naming trap (read first).** The canonical binary is **`figma-ds-cli`** (silships, npm, MIT). The npm package literally named **`figma-cli` is an UNRELATED tool** (unic/figma-cli, bin `figma`), so **NEVER `npm i -g figma-cli`**. The `figma-cli` command exists only when installed from the silships repo. This catalog uses `figma-ds-cli` as the canonical command throughout.

> **Verification note.** Commands below are illustrative and sourced from the figma-cli capability research digest, so verify any exact verb, flag, or output with `figma-ds-cli <command> --help` before relying on it. The installed `figma-ds-cli 1.2.0 create --help` lists the shape, text and group primitives as `create` subcommands, and `voice`, `chat` and `prop combine` appear in docs but were not found in source. Do NOT run `figma-ds-cli` against a live document without verifying the command and its gating class first.

---

## 1. OVERVIEW

Use this catalog as the inventory for the live `mcp-figma` surface. The numbered sections below group the skill by capability area so readers can move from a top-level summary into the per-command detail without losing the gating context.

The capability surface has one hard prerequisite and three working directions, plus an optional context pull. Everything depends on a **connection**: figma-cli drives **Figma Desktop (open with a file)**, with no Figma API key, over a local daemon. From there the **read** direction inspects and exports without changing the document, the **write** direction authors, renders, sets tokens, and imports design systems behind gates, and a small **destructive** subset deletes content behind hard confirms. Underneath the optional last direction sits the community Figma MCP, reached through this repo's Code Mode rather than by anything figma-cli ships.

A note on what stays out of scope. This skill is the terminal transport, not the measured design reference: a measured Style Reference (extracted design tokens) is produced by `sk-design-md-generator`. figma-cli does **not** ship or spawn its own MCP (source-verified zero hits), and its daemon is a private HTTP/WebSocket bridge, not an MCP server. The OFFICIAL Figma Dev Mode MCP is out of scope for this release, and only the community Framelink `figma` manual is documented as a supported optional path.

### Command class tags

Every command below carries one tag. Local exports are read-only but still write files, so they require an explicit output path and never silently overwrite.

| Class | Meaning | Default handling |
|---|---|---|
| READ-ONLY | Reads the doc or writes only export files; no document change | Safe default; exports need an explicit output path, no overwrite |
| MUTATING | Changes the Figma document or local app/config state | Gate: confirmation + explicit target |
| DESTRUCTIVE | Deletes document content or resources | Confirm + explicit target + one-line rollback |
| ARBITRARY | `eval` / `raw` / `run` can do anything | Treat as mutating; review the code/command first |

import re, subprocess
files = [
("README.md","Connecting has two modes and a sharp difference in risk. The **safe mode**, `figma-ds-cli connect --safe`, is the default. It runs the FigCli plugin bridge and patches nothing: you import `plugin/manifest.json` once, then keep `Plugins > Development > FigCli` open each session. The **yolo mode**, `figma-ds-cli connect` with no `--safe`, patches Figma Desktop's `app.asar`, codesigns on macOS and restarts Figma with a CDP debug port on 9222. It may need Full Disk Access or admin rights. It breaks when Figma updates. The skill never runs it without explicit consent and a stated rollback, which is `figma-ds-cli unpatch`."),
("README.md","The CLI's verbs fall into classes. The gate depends on the class. **Read-only** verbs are the safe default: `status`, `get`, `find`, `inspect`, the `var list` and `var find` queries, `extract`, every `export` form, the analyze and a11y audits plus dry-run variants. None of them change the Figma document, though the local exports do write files, so they still demand an explicit output path and never a silent overwrite. **Mutating** verbs change the open file and are gated behind confirmation: every `create`, `render` and token or variable verb, the bind and set families, layout verbs, variant generation, imports and the app-level `connect`, `unpatch` and `config set`. **Destructive** verbs are gated more strictly, requiring explicit confirmation, an explicit target node or file, a command preview and a one-line rollback. The destructive set is `var delete-all`, `var delete-batch`, `delete` and `remove`, `node delete`, `undo`, `unwrap`, `fj delete`, `plugins uninstall`, `dev unlink`, `component prop delete`, `grid clear` and `annotate clear`. Finally, `eval`, `raw` and `run` execute arbitrary instructions, so the skill treats them as mutating and reviews the code or command before running it, even when the prompt sounds exploratory."),
("ROUTER.md","A request that names `figma`, `figma-ds-cli`, Figma Desktop, rendering in Figma, tokens and variables, an extract to DESIGN.md, an export, a connect or a daemon reaches mcp-figma, and this router picks from the CLI command reference, the command-gating taxonomy, the optional MCP wiring, the troubleshooting reference and the paste-ready MCP assets rather than from the whole folder. Design context pulled through an opt-in Figma MCP loads the wiring doc and the paste-ready assets on top of the CLI baseline, so the MCP path never replaces the transport every other route reads. A request whose keywords barely score loads nothing and asks a disambiguation checklist instead of guessing."),
("references/troubleshooting.md","The daemon is a local **HTTP server on `127.0.0.1:3456`** (not a Unix socket), authed via the `X-Daemon-Token` header (`~/.figma-ds-cli/.daemon-token`), PID at `~/.figma-cli-daemon.pid`, with an idle timeout (~60 min) and no reboot persistence. Recovery order is always **status -> diagnose -> restart -> reconnect**."),
]
def norm(s):
    s = re.sub(r'[*_`>#|]', ' ', s)
    return re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', s).strip().lower()
for f, txt in files:
    now = norm(open(".skilled/skills/mcp-tooling/mcp-figma/"+f).read().replace("\n"," "))
    for part in re.split(r'(?<=[.;:])\s+', norm(txt)):
        part=part.strip()
        if len(part)<12: continue
        ok = part.rstrip('.;:') in now
        print(("OK  " if ok else "MISS"), f, "|", part[:110])
    print()
PY
